source: Periodic Evals run 36903600510, eval-slices (2), SCOPE EXPANSION mode routing; native public transcript

questions.question:
D1 — Which review mode should I apply to the saved-views plan?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-hgA1gj on main, reviewing PLAN.md (add saved project views).
ELI10: The plan is a solid version of the standard pattern every task tool ships: save filters + sort under a name, reopen later. The mode decides my posture: push for a bigger product, hold the line and harden it, offer optional add-ons one at a time, or cut to the smallest useful core. The main fork I found is that views are member-only, and the storage shape chosen now decides whether team-shared views are cheap later or a migration.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Expand too far and a two-week pilot feature turns into a platform project; hold too tight and the migration locks in a per-member shape that blocks shared views next quarter.
Recommendation: SELECTIVE EXPANSION because the plan is an added capability (~10-13 estimated files, under the reduction threshold) and the shared-view/owner shape question is cheapest to decide before the migration exists, while the user's stated scope stays the baseline.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
  ✅ Holds the stated per-member scope and hardens it with full error, test and observability coverage
  ✅ Puts each add-on (shared views, default view, deep links) in front of you one at a time with effort and risk
  ❌ More decisions for you to make before the deep review starts; roughly 4-6 cherry-pick questions
B) HOLD SCOPE
  ✅ Fastest path to a hardened, implementation-ready plan for exactly what you wrote
  ✅ No scope debates; review goes straight to failure modes, tests, rollout
  ❌ The member-only storage shape gets locked in without a conscious decision about shared views
C) SCOPE EXPANSION
  ✅ Designs the 12-month version now: personal + shared + default views, deep links, usage visibility
  ✅ Avoids a second migration and second UI pass later
  ❌ Likely doubles the file count and delays the two-week pilot; risks building what the pilot was meant to validate
D) SCOPE REDUCTION
  ✅ Finds the smallest thing that proves reuse: maybe bookmarkable filter URLs before any table
  ✅ Gets the pilot signal with the least code to maintain if the feature flops
  ❌ May ship something members do not perceive as "saved views", muddying the pilot metric
Net: You are trading decision time now against migration and UI rework later; A spends a little of the former to avoid the latter without committing to a bigger build.

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
options.description: Hold your scope as the baseline; I offer each expansion (shared views, default view, deep links, etc.) separately with effort and risk; you add, defer, or skip each. ✅ Keeps stated scope intact ✅ Conscious call on the storage shape before the migration ❌ 4-6 extra decisions up front

options.label: HOLD SCOPE
options.description: Preserve exactly what PLAN.md says and apply maximum rigor: failure modes, error paths, tests, observability, rollout. ✅ Fastest to an implementation-ready plan ✅ No scope debate ❌ Member-only shape locked in without an explicit decision

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION
options.description: Dream big: design the 12-month ideal now (personal + shared + default views, deep links, usage visibility). ✅ One migration, one UI pass ✅ Platform-grade result ❌ Roughly doubles scope and delays the pilot

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION
options.description: Strip to the minimum that proves members reuse views, cutting only with your approval per item. ✅ Least code if the pilot flops ✅ Fastest signal ❌ Risk of a result users do not recognize as saved views

questions.question:
D2 — E1: Should saved views be shareable with the whole project, not only private to the member who made them?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-hgA1gj on main, reviewing PLAN.md (add saved project views).
ELI10: Today's plan gives each member a private shelf of views. Every incumbent (Jira, Asana, Linear) also lets a lead publish a view the whole team opens, because the pain is usually the same view being rebuilt by many people. Adding this now means two columns (owner, visibility), one list-query change, a permission check, and a two-section picker. Adding it later means a migration plus reworking the picker after people already have private views.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Skip it and the pilot measures only solo reuse while the team-level win stays invisible; add it carelessly and a member could edit or delete a view others depend on.
Recommendation: A) Add because the storage shape is cheapest to decide before the migration exists, the permission rule is one line (owner or project admin), and shared views are the biggest multiplier on the plan's own reuse metric.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Add shared project views (recommended)
  ✅ A lead builds "Sprint blockers" once and the whole team opens it; reuse metric multiplies per member
  ✅ Schema settled now (owner + visibility), no second migration or picker rework later
  ❌ Adds a permission surface: who may edit/delete a project view must be tested, including non-owner denial
B) Defer to TODOS.md
  ✅ Keeps the pilot focused on the per-member behavior PLAN.md describes
  ✅ Review will still flag the owner/visibility column so the table is forward-compatible
  ❌ Picker and list endpoint get reworked when sharing lands; private views already exist by then
C) Skip
  ✅ Smallest permission surface: owner-only, no admin override to reason about
  ✅ Zero implementation work beyond PLAN.md
  ❌ Locks in member-only shape; every member rebuilds the lead's view, which is the original pain
Net: Two columns and one guard now versus a migration and a picker rework later; the pilot metric gets stronger either way you add it.

options.label: Add shared project views (recommended)
options.description: Add owner + visibility (private/project) to saved_views; list returns own private + project views; owner or project admin may edit/delete; picker shows Mine / Project. Effort M (human ~2 days / CC ~30 min), risk medium, reuses existing membership/admin role check; verification: visibility filtering, admin edit allowed, non-owner denied, access rules unchanged. ✅ Lead saves once, team opens it ✅ Schema settled before migration ❌ New permission surface to test

options.label: Defer to TODOS.md
options.description: Keep views private for the pilot; record shared views in TODOS.md with this context. Effort S (zero implementation work now), risk low; review will still raise the owner/visibility column as a forward-compatibility finding. ✅ Pilot stays focused on per-member reuse ✅ Nothing to build now ❌ Picker and list endpoint rework later

options.label: Skip
options.description: Views stay member-only with no TODO. Effort S (zero implementation work), risk low; verification unchanged from PLAN.md. ✅ Smallest permission surface ✅ No extra work ❌ Member-only shape locked in; lead's view rebuilt by every member

questions.question:
D3 — E3: Should every saved view be a deep link, with the URL carrying the view id and the full filter + sort state?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-hgA1gj on main, reviewing PLAN.md (add saved project views).
ELI10: Right now the plan says the picker applies a view, but nothing says what the browser address shows. If the URL carries the view id and the filter state, then reload keeps what you had, the back button works, and a view is shareable by copying the address into chat. Without it, a shared view (E1, just accepted) can only be reached by finding it in the picker, and a refresh drops you back to the unfiltered list.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Skip it and shared views lose their easiest distribution channel and refresh/back behave surprisingly; add it and the implementer must define a stable serialization and handle unknown or deleted view ids in links.
Recommendation: A) Add because E1 made views a team artifact and a link is how teams pass artifacts around; the work is mostly plumbing the state the picker already has into the query string, and it makes "reopen later" survive refresh for free.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Add deep-linkable views and URL state (recommended)
  ✅ Paste a link in chat and a teammate sees exactly the same tasks; refresh and back button keep the view
  ✅ Gives the save action a stable, testable serialization instead of reading transient UI state
  ❌ Must handle unknown, deleted, or foreign-project view ids in links with a clear not-found state
B) Defer to TODOS.md
  ✅ Keeps the pilot to picker-driven reuse, closer to what PLAN.md describes
  ✅ Serialization can be designed later with real usage data on which filters matter
  ❌ Refresh drops the view and shared views are only discoverable through the picker during the pilot
C) Skip
  ✅ Zero implementation work; picker remains the only entry point
  ✅ No URL compatibility to maintain if filter options change
  ❌ No shareable links, no refresh persistence, back button ignores view changes
Net: One serialization layer now buys sharing, refresh, and back-button behavior; skipping it leaves E1 half as useful.

options.label: Add deep-linkable views and URL state (recommended)
options.description: URL query string is the source of truth for view id + filters + sort; opening a view updates the URL and pushes history; links open the same tasks for any member with project access; unknown/deleted/foreign view id shows a not-found empty state. Effort S–M (human ~1 day / CC ~20 min), risk low, reuses existing router/query parsing; verification: URL round-trip, bad view id, back/forward, foreign-project id denied. ✅ Shareable links, refresh and back work ✅ Stable serialization for save ❌ Bad-link states to handle

options.label: Defer to TODOS.md
options.description: Keep picker-only application for the pilot; record URL state + deep links in TODOS.md with this context. Effort S (zero implementation work now), risk low. ✅ Pilot stays picker-focused ✅ Design serialization with usage data ❌ Refresh loses view; shared views only via picker

options.label: Skip
options.description: No URL involvement and no TODO. Effort S (zero implementation work), risk low; verification unchanged. ✅ No extra work ✅ No URL contract to maintain ❌ No links, no refresh persistence, back button ignores views
